NNSA provides capabilities that can be used at international borders to help detect and deter smuggling. Within the US, this capability is managed by DHS, but the NNSA mission requires that the technology provided cannot be export-controlled. The hardware currently used in this application area are radiation portals used to scan trucks, containers, ships and other transportation means, along with handheld and backpack instruments. Inspections can have multiple stages, e.g., if an initial detection is made, the object is often subjected to a more comprehensive secondary inspection with better instruments and could even involve an intrusive tertiary inspection / strip down of a shipping container and/or the transport. The instruments used in these inspections, as well as the entire security infrastructure within which the instruments are used and the associated CONOPs, are often subjected to simulations studies. The personnel operating these instruments are border guards, not technical experts, and therefore the technology needs to be simple to operate and/or be largely automated. One possible new application of a mobile SDF platform would be to automate secondary inspections. These inspections are currently performed using X-ray scanners capable of scanning entire trucks or shipping containers.
